description.text: Semiquincentennial Tourism and Access to Recreation Sites Act or the STARS Act This bill directs the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service to designate September 17, 2026, as an entrance-fee free date in honor of the 250th anniversary of the United States of America. On that date, Interior must waive (1) the entrance fees for all visitors of National Park Service or National Wildlife Refuge System sites; and (2) the standard amenity recreation fees for all visitors to each site managed by the Bureau of Land Management or the Bureau of Reclamation. The Forest Service must waive the standard amenity recreation fees on that date for all visitors to sites it manages.

latestAction.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

aiDescription.summary: The STARS Act waives entrance and standard amenity recreation fees on September 17, 2026, making recreation sites free. It covers National Park System and National Wildlife Refuge units that charge entrance fees, and Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation, and Forest Service sites charging standard amenity fees.

impact.summary: On September 17, 2026 the STARS Act waives entrance fees at National Park Service and National Wildlife Refuge System units. It also waives amenity recreation fees at Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation, and Forest Service sites, affecting all visitors and agency fee receipts.
